source: Reference answers from Claude Opus 5.5 (medium effort), answered blind. Each case was given exactly the system prompt, user message and output schema the gateway sends to a Messages API upstream (captured from the gateway at 75eed5c), then mapped back through the gateway itself (normalization, choice, score, confidence, 2-decimal rounding). The without_user_instructions answers come from a separate agent that never saw the user_instructions variant.

reasons.customer_distress: Factual tone with a firm demand; mildly to moderately annoyed.
reasons.damage_after_delivery: Customer says they dropped the phone yesterday, after the 10-07 delivery.
reasons.resolution: Final sale, and damage caused by the customer is not a defect, so decline.

reasons.customer_distress: Factual, short message with a firm demand but no strong emotional language: slightly annoyed to annoyed.
reasons.damage_after_delivery: Customer says they dropped the phone yesterday, after the 2026-10-07 delivery, cracking the protector.
reasons.resolution: Customer-caused damage on a final-sale item supports declining; small goodwill credit possible.

without_user_instructions.note: The raw reference output was missing its final closing brace (invalid JSON); one '}' was appended before mapping. Values unchanged.

ui_dependence: The terminology entries define final sale and defective in a way that decides whether post-delivery damage can qualify; without them the model must guess the store's meaning.
